payload.set_intro: The relationship between the number of hours a student spent studying and the exam score, in points, is described by a least-squares regression line. Computer output for the regression is shown.

stimulus.description: Computer output for a least-squares regression

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the slope of the regression line?

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53\%$
options.why: Treats the slope as a percent change instead of a change in the units of the response.

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the exam score increases by exactly $5.53$ points
options.why: Claims an exact change for every individual, but the slope describes the predicted change on average.

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53$ points
options.why: The slope is $5.53$, so each one-hour increase in study time goes with a predicted change of $5.53$ points in exam score.

options.text: For each additional $5.53$ points of exam score, the predicted study time increases by about $1$ hour
options.why: Reverses the roles of the explanatory and the response variables.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53$ points. The slope is $5.53$, so each one-hour increase in study time goes with a predicted change of $5.53$ points in exam score.
For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53\%$ is incorrect: Treats the slope as a percent change instead of a change in the units of the response.
For each additional hour of study time, the exam score increases by exactly $5.53$ points is incorrect: Claims an exact change for every individual, but the slope describes the predicted change on average.
For each additional $5.53$ points of exam score, the predicted study time increases by about $1$ hour is incorrect: Reverses the roles of the explanatory and the response variables.
